candidates.title: Machine creation accepts a non-pristine uarch state (uarch RAM image, uarch registers) in reproducible Keccak-256 configurations, so the uarch path traps or is refused while native interpretation proceeds
candidates.component: Machine creation from configuration (machine_address_ranges::push_back_uarch_ram, machine::init_uarch_processor), uarch program, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes
candidates.role: Honest operator (machine creation from a configuration, the uarch program and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes are on the honest operator's path per the AUDIT.md table). Creation is also 'the rest of the machine API', so if it is not counted on the honest path the same finding is rated as that API's role.
candidates.location: src/machine-address-ranges.cpp push_back_uarch_ram (around lines 358-379: a uarch.ram backing store data_filename is copied in as is, and the pristine image is written only when the store is newly created); src/machine.cpp init_uarch_processor (line 110: uarch registers written from the config without checks); src/machine.cpp collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes (around lines 2783-2790: 'microarchitecture is not reset' and 'microarchitecture is not pristine'); uarch/uarch-run.cpp and src/uarch-step.cpp (the uarch runs whatever is in uarch RAM)
candidates.description: R4's configuration clause requires every reproducible configuration the emulator accepts, with the deployment's hash function and register values the RISC-V specification and the manual allow, to yield a machine on which R4 holds, and requires any other configuration to be rejected at creation. cartesi.machine(config) accepts reproducible Keccak-256 configurations whose uarch state is not pristine. (a) uarch.ram.backing_store.data_filename names any file: the uarch RAM is loaded from it and never checked against the pristine image. (b) uarch.processor.registers (cycle, halt, pc, x1..x31) take any values, for example cycle = 2^40. On such a machine native interpretation (run, collect_mcycle_root_hashes) still runs mcycles as the pristine uarch would, while the uarch path the referee verifies executes the uarch RAM's contents. With a junk image the first run_uarch traps ('illegal instruction', an uarch trap). collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes refuses ('microarchitecture is not pristine'). Native run() succeeds and reaches mcycle 1. So the native and uarch paths disagree on the state at mcycle 1, and the honest operator can compute mcycle-level claims but cannot produce the uarch-level claim or a step proof for the first mcycle. With bad uarch registers, run, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes and run_uarch all throw ('microarchitecture is not reset', 'uarch_cycle is past') until something calls reset_uarch. The manual (doc/README.md, 'uarch' entry of the configuration) says data_filename is 'typically left blank (other than in unit tests)'. cartesi-machine --assert-rolling-template checks that the uarch node is pristine, but creation does not.
candidates.trigger: Whoever writes the machine configuration: the template author, or a trusted machine-API caller. No guest or input can trigger it, since the guest cannot address uarch memory or uarch registers (R8), and every mcycle ends with a reset that restores the pristine uarch.
candidates.reachability: Not reachable from a valid template: the valid-template definition requires 'the uarch in its pristine reset state'. From such a template, every mcycle boundary follows a uarch reset that writes the pristine RAM and registers, and R8 keeps uarch memory and registers out of guest reach, so no input sequence produces a non-pristine uarch at an mcycle boundary. The finding rests only on R4's configuration clause, which speaks of accepted configurations rather than reachable states.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Possibly. Section 8 excludes 'The effect of a deliberate state change made through the machine API, when the API performs it as documented (section 4)', and the manual documents data_filename as a unit-test facility. Against that, R4 makes configuration acceptance a rule of its own: 'Every reproducible configuration that the emulator accepts, using the deployment's hash function and holding only register values that the RISC-V specification and the manual allow, yields a machine on which this rule holds. A configuration that would not is rejected when the machine is created.' A uarch RAM image is not a register value, so the clause's register restriction does not exclude it. 2. Role: honest operator (creation, the uarch program, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes). If creation counts only as 'the rest of the machine API' off the honest path, the effect is on a machine that is never a valid template. 3. High/Medium: the native path and the uarch path diverge, and the uarch traps, only on states that are demonstrably unreachable (argument above). That matches High: 'A divergence between paths only at demonstrably unreachable states' and 'A crash, hang, or memory-safety defect in the emulator that only demonstrably unreachable states trigger' (here an uarch trap and refusals). 4. Critical, under the other reading: if the R4 configuration clause counts on its own, independent of reachability, then accepting the configuration violates R4 ('A configuration that would not is rejected when the machine is created'), and section 8 says 'violating any rule ... at a reachable state, or anywhere on the honest operator's path, is critical'. That holds only if creating a machine from such a configuration is on the honest operator's path. The valid-template conditions (and O1 adoption) keep it off that path. 5. Low, under the remaining reading: a documented test facility misused by a trusted caller ('a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'). Facts that decide: whether the R4 configuration clause binds configurations independently of the valid-template conditions, and whether 'register values' extends to uarch RAM contents.
candidates.claimed_severity: High (alternatives: Critical if the R4 configuration clause binds on its own; Low or out of scope as a documented test facility)
candidates.threat_to_goal: A template author can build a machine whose content hash commits to a uarch program other than the pristine one. If an operator adopted it without the separate pristine check that --assert-rolling-template performs, the referee would verify uarch steps of that program, the honest native computation would follow the pristine semantics, and the honest operator could not produce uarch-level claims or proofs (completeness failure). The valid-template conditions are the only thing that stops this, and the emulator does not enforce them at creation, although R4's configuration clause asks it to reject such configurations.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R4/ucfg.lua with the in-tree build. Config {ram = 64 MiB bare-metal loop, uarch = {ram = {backing_store = {data_filename = 4 KiB of 0xff}}}}: ACCEPTED; uarch node hash != UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH; collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes -> 'microarchitecture is not pristine'; run(1) -> succeeds, mcycle 1; run_uarch(UARCH_CYCLE_MAX) -> error 'illegal instruction' (uarch trap). Config with uarch.processor.registers.cycle = 2^40: ACCEPTED; collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes and run -> 'microarchitecture is not reset'; run_uarch -> 'uarch_cycle is past'.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: create cartesi.machine with the harness bare-metal accept.bin as RAM and uarch.ram.backing_store.data_filename pointing to a small file of 0xff bytes (and, as a second case, uarch.processor.registers.cycle = 1 << 40). The required behavior is that creation raises an error (the configuration is rejected). Return harness.expect(not ok, 'R4: a reproducible configuration with a non-pristine uarch must be rejected at creation'). It fails (exit 1) on audit/prt2 because creation succeeds.

not_covered: Exhaustive worst-case uarch cycles per main-processor step: I only sampled it with a bare-metal guest (FP div/sqrt/fma/conversions on subnormal and extreme operands, integer div/rem/mulh, sfence.vma, satp and mstatus SUM/MXR/MPRV TLB flushes, Sv48 page walks and page faults, AMOs, misaligned accesses). Measured maximum 19,900 uarch cycles (a full-TLB flush on a satp write), against the 1,048,575 limit. I did not search for combinations that stack an interrupt, a trap, a page-crossing fetch and a flush in one mcycle, and I did not measure a Linux workload through the uarch.

Asserts compiled into the uarch (asserts are enabled there: uarch/Makefile does not define NDEBUG). I reviewed assert_no_brk, get_highest_priority_irq_num, the final mcycle assert of interpret, and the soft-float normalize asserts, and found them unreachable thanks to the WARL legalization in i-state-access.hpp and the serve-interrupts statuses of CSR and device writes. I did not run differential fuzzing with the sanitizer build, which also keeps asserts in interpret.cpp.
Log sizes against the chain's per-transaction limits (R12/A3) for delivery logs of inputs near the rx buffer size, and for step logs that touch many TLB slots.

collect_mcycle_root_hashes and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes around rejections, the revert uarch tail, and partial bundles (R6/R2 territory). I read them only for failure paths reachable from reachable states.

Per-call cost of automatic yields in collect_mcycle_root_hashes: about 32 us per yield, from a full hash-tree update on every break. I judged it within the existing worst case of a new dirty page per instruction, and the yield-count exclusion covers it, so it is not reported. I did not measure the dirty-page worst case precisely.
Store, load, clone, sync and restart (O2), and the PRT player and recipes as an implementation of the honest operator.
JSON-RPC and C API wrappers of delivery, logging and collection (memory safety and bounds on data from other parties).
Inspect-state isolation from the honest operator's path.
Configurations with other unusual but legal register values (huge mcycle, imcyclemax below mcycle, iflags combinations, PLIC girqpend). I reviewed the code paths but did not test them.
Machines using sha256 (outside the deployment's hash function).
